sources.title: Fougeron & Smith (1993), French: Illustrations of the IPA
sources.whatItSupports: Parisian vowel/consonant inventory, mid-vowel distributions, nasal notation and rhotic variation.
sources.limitations: Descriptive reference, not learner outcome evidence or certification of this word bank.

sources.title: Levy (2009), On the assimilation-discrimination relationship in American English adults’ French vowel learning
sources.whatItSupports: American-English listeners, /y–u/ difficulty and consonantal-context effects.
sources.limitations: Nonword frames /rabVp/ and /radVt/; not a source of real-word stimuli or a test of this product’s ABX method.

sources.title: Inceoglu (2016), Effects of perceptual training on second language vowel perception and production
sources.whatItSupports: French nasal-vowel training of 60 intermediate American-English learners; auditory and audiovisual groups improved.
sources.limitations: Author abstract and later author discussion checked; full stimulus appendix not recovered. No words are attributed to this experiment.

sources.title: Inceoglu (2022), A web-based high variability phonetic training application for French vowels
sources.whatItSupports: Explicit familiarization words for the Ouïe application, tagged individually below.
sources.limitations: Application-development paper, not a controlled efficacy trial. Familiarization examples are not its complete 181-word training inventory. Training uses phoneme identification with IPA choices. Full-word IPA/glosses here are editorial.

sources.title: Kingston (2003), Learning Foreign Vowels
sources.whatItSupports: American-English learners, 12 German nonlow vowel categories, identification training with five speakers and varied consonantal frames.
sources.limitations: Words and pseudowords in stressed CVCn frames. No full lexical bank recovered. Inventory coverage does not prove every selected binary contrast below was separately trained.

sources.title: Gao et al. (2019), Perception of German tense and lax vowel contrast by Chinese learners
sources.whatItSupports: Seven tense/lax vowel pairs; Mandarin-Chinese listeners and German controls; quality/duration manipulations.
sources.limitations: Perception experiment with synthesized words, not HVPT. Full 70-word list not recovered; no word below is claimed as its stimulus.

sources.title: Riedinger et al. (2021), Asymmetries in Accessing Vowel Representations Are Driven by Phonological and Acoustic Properties
sources.whatItSupports: Ten named words forming five long-vowel minimal pairs in native German perception experiments.
sources.limitations: Native listeners, one speaker; not L2 efficacy evidence. Full-word IPA here is editorial; table Stieg is normalized to verb stieg.
sources.license: CC BY, stated by publisher; no recordings copied.

sources.title: Möbius & Trouvain (2014), Phonology, Saarland University
sources.whatItSupports: German minimal-pair examples, inventories, contextual ich/ach allophones and final neutralization.
sources.limitations: University phonetics teaching material, not an L2 outcome experiment.

gaps: Text-only draft for owner/native review. No audio generated, approved or evaluated.
Common-word status is an editorial suitability screen, not a measured frequency threshold. Historically integrated ordinary words retained; etymology alone is not exclusion.
Every contrast has at least four spellings per side and one context with four per side. Smaller secondary groups remain; homophones do not imply acoustic diversity.
Inherited dictionary sources include lookup targets not all freshly opened. New entries were directly checked; this is not full independent certification of every inherited word.
French /ø–œ/ common-word coverage retains strong coda/dialect cues. Do not present these pools as a coda-controlled minimal-pair assessment.
French /ɲ/ may surface [nj]; mid vowels and jeûne/jeune vary regionally. Selected /a–ɑ/ merger explains tasse/vase normalization. Do not silently change dialect.

English reference varieties are explicit General American and Standard Southern British. SSBE now has 22 selected comparisons in its separate bank; no country-wide accent or full British coverage claimed.
German schwa/rhotic normalization explicit. Löffel normalized from /ˈlœfl/ to /ˈlœfəl/. Existing spulen exact-IPA gap remains.

Backlog requiring further primary L2 evidence and pools: English /tʃ–dʒ/, FACE/DRESS, GOAT/LOT, stress/clusters; German stop voicing/aspiration, /f–v/, affricates/diphthongs; French oral /ɔ/ versus nasal /ɔ̃/, glides/liaison/schwa. Not universally difficult contrasts.
New /θ–t/ and /ɛ–ɛ̃/ entries are inventory candidates, not inspected L2 stimuli. No new word gains a stimulusSourceId. No ABX-superiority claim.
Retained documented stimulus provenance preserved; vocabulary removed from practice remains in its historical source, not in these pools.
